# SANS Institute

> SANS Institute is the most trusted resource for cybersecurity training, certifications and research, offering 85+ hands-on courses across offensive security, cyber defense, digital forensics, cloud security, industrial control systems, and leadership, taught by practitioners actively working in the field. SANS is the primary training partner for GIAC, the industry's most rigorous hands-on cybersecurity certification body, and operates the Internet Storm Center, a volunteer-staffed threat monitoring service running since 2001.

Version 1.0, last updated 2026-10. A full list of pages is available in the [sitemap](https://www.sans.org/sitemap-index.xml).

## Courses

- [All Cybersecurity Courses](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-courses): Full catalog of SANS training courses, filterable by focus area, format, and skill level.
- [Ways to Train](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-training-formats): In-person, Live Online, and OnDemand (self-paced) training formats.
- [Cybersecurity Skills Roadmap](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-skills-roadmap): Recommended course sequencing by role and skill level.
- [By Job Role](https://www.sans.org/job-roles): Course and certification paths mapped to specific job roles.
- [Free Course Previews](https://www.sans.org/course-preview): Free hour-long previews of 70+ SANS courses.

## Featured Courses: AI & Agentic Security

- [SEC545: GenAI and LLM Application Security](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-courses/genai-llm-application-security): Securing generative AI applications and LLM development pipelines.
- [SEC535: Offensive AI - Attack Tools and Techniques](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-courses/offensive-ai-attack-tools-techniques): Offensive security techniques applied to AI systems.
- [SEC536: Adversarial AI](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-courses/adversarial-ai): Penetration testing AI systems and models.
- [SEC598: AI and Security Automation for Red, Blue, and Purple Teams](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-courses/ai-security-automation): Applying AI and automation across offensive, defensive, and cloud security operations.
- [SEC546: Securing Agentic AI](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-courses/securing-agentic-ai): Security practices specific to autonomous, agentic AI systems.
- [SEC411: AI Security Principles & Practices](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-courses/ai-security-principles-practices): Foundational AI security concepts for practitioners.

## Featured Courses: Core Disciplines

- [SEC401: Security Essentials](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-courses/security-essentials): Foundational cyber defense course covering access control, incident handling, and defense in depth.
- [SEC504: Hacker Techniques, Incident Handling](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-courses/hacker-techniques-incident-handling): Incident handling and attacker technique fundamentals.
- [SEC560: Enterprise Penetration Testing](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-courses/enterprise-penetration-testing): Enterprise-scale penetration testing methodology.
- [FOR500: Windows Forensic Analysis](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-courses/windows-forensic-analysis): Core digital forensics course for Windows environments.
- [FOR509: Enterprise Incident Response & Threat Hunting](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-courses/enterprise-incident-response-threat-hunting): Enterprise-scale incident response and threat hunting.
- [SEC549: Cloud Security Architecture](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-courses/cloud-security-architecture): Zero-trust strategies and cloud architecture security.
- [LDR512: Security Leadership Essentials for Managers](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-courses/security-leadership-essentials-for-managers): Leadership fundamentals for security managers.
- [FOR578: Cyber Threat Intelligence](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-courses/cyber-threat-intelligence): Threat intelligence collection and analysis.

## Focus Areas

- [AI Security](https://www.sans.org/cybersecurity-focus-areas/ai): Training on defending AI systems, securing agentic AI, and using AI to enhance security operations.
- [Offensive Operations](https://www.sans.org/cybersecurity-focus-areas/offensive-operations): Penetration testing, red teaming, and exploit development courses.
- [Cyber Defense](https://www.sans.org/cybersecurity-focus-areas/cyber-defense): Security operations, detection engineering, and defensive architecture.
- [Digital Forensics & Incident Response](https://www.sans.org/cybersecurity-focus-areas/digital-forensics-incident-response): DFIR training and incident handling.
- [Cloud Security](https://www.sans.org/cybersecurity-focus-areas/cloud-security): Securing cloud infrastructure and cloud-native environments.
- [Industrial Control Systems Security](https://www.sans.org/cybersecurity-focus-areas/industrial-control-systems-security): OT/ICS and SCADA security training.
- [Cybersecurity Leadership](https://www.sans.org/cybersecurity-focus-areas/leadership): Training for security managers and executives.
- [OSINT](https://www.sans.org/cybersecurity-focus-areas/osint): Open-source intelligence gathering and analysis.

## GIAC Certifications

- [GIAC Certifications Overview](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-certifications): Full catalog of 60+ hands-on, practitioner-focused cybersecurity certifications.
- [Why Certify](https://www.sans.org/blog/be-ready-be-resilient-hands-on-cybersecurity-training-skill-validation-for-real-world-threats): Why GIAC certification is a recognized, rigorous standard.

## Featured GIAC Certifications: AI

- [GIAC AI Platform Security (GAIPS)](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-certifications/ai-security-platform-security-gaips): Auditing and securing GenAI applications and LLM development pipelines.
- [GIAC AI Security Automation Engineer (GASAE)](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-certifications/ai-security-automation-engineer-gasae): Applying AI and automation across offensive, defensive, and cloud security operations.
- [GIAC Offensive AI Analyst (GOAA)](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-certifications/offensive-ai-analyst-goaa): Applying offensive AI techniques to modern cybersecurity challenges.

## Featured GIAC Certifications: Core Disciplines

- [GIAC Red Team Professional (GRTP)](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-certifications/red-team-professional-grtp): Red team engagement skills from start to finish.
- [GIAC Cloud Security Architecture and Design (GCAD)](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-certifications/cloud-security-architecture-design-gcad): Zero-trust and cloud architecture security.
- [GIAC Enterprise Incident Response (GEIR)](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-certifications/enterprise-incident-responder-geir): Enterprise-scale incident response tools and methodology.
- [GIAC Cyber Incident Leader (GCIL)](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-certifications/cyber-incident-leader-gcil): Leading teams through incident handling and remediation.

## Training Events & Summits

- [Training Events & Summits](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-training-events): Full calendar of in person and Live Online training events worldwide.
- [Free Training Events](https://www.sans.org/free-cybersecurity-events): Free workshops, webinars, and local events.
- [SANSFIRE](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-training-events/sansfire-2027): SANS's flagship annual multi-course training event.
- [Cyber Defense Initiative (CDI)](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-training-events/cyber-defense-initiative-2026): Major year-end multi-course training event in Washington, D.C.
- [AI Cybersecurity Summit](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-training-events/ai-summit-fall-2026): Summit on securing, evaluating, and governing AI systems, including agentic AI.
- [DFIR Summit](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-training-events/digital-forensics-summit-2026): Annual Digital Forensics and Incident Response summit.
- [ICS Security Summit](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-training-events/ics-security-summit-2027): Industrial control systems/OT security summit.
- [Security Awareness Summit](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-training-events/ldr433-awareness-summit-2026): Summit focused on security culture and human risk management.
- [SANS 2027](https://www.sans.org/cyber-security-training-events/sans-2027): Large annual multi-course training event.

## For Organizations

- [For Organizations Overview](https://www.sans.org/for-organizations): Team training, leadership development, and workforce risk programs.
- [Workforce Security & Risk Training](https://www.sans.org/for-organizations/workforce): End-user and role-based security awareness training.
- [Group Purchasing](https://www.sans.org/for-organizations/team-development/group-purchasing): Bulk/team training purchase options.
- [Private & Custom Training](https://www.sans.org/for-organizations/team-development/private-training): Custom training programs for organizations.
- [Public Sector](https://www.sans.org/for-organizations/public-sector): Training for government, defense, and education.

## Research

- [White Papers](https://www.sans.org/white-papers): Full library of SANS-authored research on threats, defense strategy, and industry surveys.
- [Reading Room](https://www.sans.org/reading-room): Community-contributed security research.
- [Blog](https://www.sans.org/blog): Analysis and commentary from SANS instructors and staff.
- [Webcasts](https://www.sans.org/webcasts): Free live and recorded webcasts on current security topics.
- [Posters & Cheat Sheets](https://www.sans.org/posters): Free quick-reference security resources.

## Featured Research: AI & Agentic Security

- [Securing the Agentic Cloud](https://www.sans.org/white-papers/securing-the-agentic-cloud): Detection, zero trust, governance, and architecture strategies for agentic AI in the cloud.
- [Zero Trust and AI in Cloud Environments: Securing Autonomous Agents and Modern Workloads](https://www.sans.org/white-papers/zero-trust-ai-cloud-environments-securing-autonomous-agents-modern-workloads): Zero Trust framework for AI agents built on human oversight, dynamically limited privileges, and centralized logging.
- [Agentic Security: Detection and Response at Machine Speed](https://www.sans.org/white-papers/agentic-security-detection-response-machine-speed): Closing detection gaps for autonomous agents and automating containment and remediation in seconds.
- [Quantifying Agentic Misalignment in Multi-Agent Systems](https://www.sans.org/white-papers/quantifying-agentic-misalignment-multi-agent-systems): 1,500-run study of unsafe behavior in supervisor/sub-agent setups, with findings on prompt injection and runtime controls.
- [Bot or Not? Detecting AI-Driven Web Traffic Using Network Metadata Analysis](https://www.sans.org/white-papers/bot-not-detecting-ai-driven-web-traffic-using-network-metadata-analysis): Lightweight network-metadata method for detecting AI-driven web traffic.
- [Assessing the Feasibility and Effectiveness of AI in CTI-Driven Threat Hunting](https://www.sans.org/white-papers/assessing-feasibility-effectiveness-ai-cti-driven-threat-hunting): Tests three commercial LLMs on extracting indicators from threat reports and generating KQL and CQL hunting queries.

## Featured Blogs: AI & Agentic Security

- [Securing AI, Benefiting from AI](https://www.sans.org/blog/securing-ai-benefit-from-ai): Balancing AI adoption with AI-specific security risk.
- [Why We Built the AI Defense Matrix, and What We Need from You Now](https://www.sans.org/blog/why-we-built-the-ai-defense-matrix-and-what-we-need-from-you-now): Free framework from Lenny Zeltser and Sounil Yu that maps AI asset classes to NIST CSF functions to expose control gaps and owners.
- [Frontier AI: Vulnerability Management's System Revolution](https://www.sans.org/blog/frontier-aivulnerability-managements-system-revolution): Why frontier AI models push vulnerability programs toward exposure management and faster, automated patching.
- [How to Integrate AI into the Modern SOC](https://www.sans.org/blog/how-integrate-ai-modern-soc): Applying AI within security operations workflows.
- [AI-Powered Ransomware: How Threat Actors Weaponize AI](https://www.sans.org/blog/ai-powered-ransomware-how-threat-actors-weaponize-ai-across-attack-lifecycle): How adversaries use AI across the ransomware attack lifecycle.
- [SANS Launches First Hackathon on Autonomous Incident Response](https://www.sans.org/blog/sans-launches-first-hackathon-autonomous-incident-response): SANS research initiative on AI-driven, autonomous incident response.
- [Protocol SIFT: Experimental Research Initiative in AI-Assisted DFIR](https://www.sans.org/blog/protocol-sift-experimental-research-initiative-ai-assisted-dfir): Research initiative applying AI assistance to digital forensics.
- [AI Vulnerability Discovery: Hype vs. Reality](https://www.sans.org/blog/sans-critical-advisory-bugbusters-ai-vulnerability-discovery-hype-vs-reality): Critical assessment of AI-driven vulnerability discovery claims.

## About

- [About SANS](https://www.sans.org/about): Organization background and mission.
- [Instructors](https://www.sans.org/instructors): SANS's practitioner-instructor network.
- [Contact](https://www.sans.org/about/contact): Contact and training-advisor inquiries.

Insights From The Experts

Why AI Confidence Is Not Validation

AI is already part of digital forensics and incident response work, with or without a policy in place to govern it. The issue is that these tools are growing more confident in their own output faster than practitioners are developing reliable ways to verify it. Without governance models and validation standards in place, that gap compounds and rarely stays contained to a workstation: an unverified finding can end up in a forensic report, a deposition, or in court.
